thought.text: The container has the repo at `/workspaces/workspace`. Now I'll replicate the devcontainer features: Go (for forego), Node, pnpm, postgres-client, and apt packages:

reasoning_content:
The repository is located at /workspaces/workspace (because the volume maps host's / to /workspaces). In the actual devcontainer, workspaceFolder is /workspaces/${localWorkspaceFolderBasename}, and the volume mapping is ../../..:/workspaces. Since the host path is /workspace, ../../.. from .devcontainer/default would be... wait, the volume in compose.yaml is ../../.., which is three levels up from .devcontainer/default, i.e., it points to / on the host. This is a bug in their configuration — it assumes the repository is at /workspaces/<basename>, and ../../.. resolves to /workspaces. On this machine, the repository is at /workspace, so the mount ends up mapping host's / to /workspaces, placing the repository at /workspaces/workspace.

I can work around this by running commands inside the container with the working directory set to /workspaces/workspace. The container's internal configuration (env vars, paths) mostly uses relative paths (the bin path feature adds /workspaces/<name>/bin to PATH). I can just export PATH manually.

Actually, a cleaner approach: I can create a bind mount to make /workspaces/zammad work. But I can't add a volume to a running container. Alternative: mount a volume via another container? Even simpler: just work in /workspaces/workspace inside the container and adjust PATH. The add-bin-path feature's install.sh writes /etc/profile.d/add_bin_path.sh with the correct path. I can create that file myself.

Plan inside the container:
1. Install Go (needed for forego) — use mise? The base image uses mise for ruby. The devcontainer feature `go` installs Go via apt or a binary. Let me check what the go feature does — probably a binary install to /usr/local/go. I can manually download the go binary.
2. Install node via the node feature — it uses mise or a node version manager. Actually, the rails devcontainer ruby image already has mise, and the node feature (v2) with installYarnUsingApt=false... installs Node via mise or apt. Let me try mise use node@24.

Wait — the node feature in the rails/devcontainer image... anyway, let me try installing via mise: `mise use -g node@24` etc. pnpm via corepack or mise.

First, let me check what's in the image's mise and whether there's internet access from within the container.

action.command: docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -lc 'cd /workspaces/workspace && ls ~/.local/share/mise/installs/; mise which ruby 2>&1; timeout 20 curl -sI https://registry.npmjs.org/ | head -2'
